results.content: Characterizing Flavors Increase Youth and Young Adult Experimentation With Tobacco Products, Including Cigars, and Make Progression to Regular Tobacco Use More Likely Real-World Experiences Demonstrate That Restricting Characterizing Flavors in Tobacco Products, Including Cigars, Decreases Tobacco Use Docket Title | Document ID | Comments || Tobacco Product Standard for Characterizing Flavors in Cigars | FDA-2021-N-1309-0001 | 71,656 |  | The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or Agency) is proposing a tobacco product standard that would prohibit characterizing flavors (other than tobacco) in all cigars and their components and parts. (a) This part sets out a tobacco product standard under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act regarding the use of characterizing flavors in cigars. 1.  Throughout this document, FDA uses the terms “tobacco-flavored,” “non-flavored,” and “unflavored.” FDA relies on the specific term used by researchers when citing to individual studies; however, FDA generally considers a cigar that does not have a characterizing flavor other than tobacco to be “tobacco-flavored.”
